The test image shows a tomato field with plants appearing stunted/bushy with somewhat distorted growth - whole plant view. Top candidates from the whole_plant index: Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt.

Now viewing one reference from each of 4 different candidate classes:

Strong match. The CMV reference (Bugwood_1568047) is consecutive with the test image (1568048) — same field setting, same stunted/bushy spreading plant appearance. Now viewing 3 more from different classes.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image (1568048):** Field-wide rows of tomato plants showing stunted, bushy, spreading growth — no obvious wilting or necrosis.
- **CMV reference (1568047):** Consecutive Bugwood ID, same field setting, same stunted/bushy plant morphology. Extremely similar. CMV description matches: "stunted, bushy" plants.
- **TSWV:** Shows close-up bronzing and dark necrotic spots — doesn't match the field-wide stunted pattern.
- **Bacterial Wilt:** Shows drooping/collapsing plants — clearly different.
- **Verticillium Wilt:** Shows V-shaped yellowing on individual leaves — clearly different.

The consecutive Bugwood IDs (1568047/1568048) combined with the identical field setting and stunted/bushy whole-plant morphology make Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus the clear match.
